messages:
incident-bot: Paging: SEV2 - router tail latency spike in eu-west-2 affecting streaming responses. p99 > 4s, p95 ~ 320ms. Automatically opened bridge: https://calls.redwood/bridge/5510009876 :rotating_light:
oncall-amber: I’m on it, joining bridge in 30s. Collecting traces and flame graphs now.
oncall-amber: Quick check: any deploys to routing or balancer in last 30m? @infra-bot can you confirm?
infra-bot: Recent CI: rb-router-weight-rollout v2.3.1 merged 7m ago, pushed to eu-* zones (canary->partial). No other infra deploys in last hour.
dinesh: That rollout included a change to affinity bucketing + weight decay. Noted at code review: fallback route ordering changed (local preferred -> cost-based). Could cause more cross-shard fanout.
maria: Confirming symptoms: higher inter-zone hops in traces, request stream stalls when a call crosses to a hot partition. Seeing increased KV cache misses during those hops.
kevin: p95 numbers: 320ms. p99 numbers from Grafana (last 15m): 4.5s. Streaming stalls count increased 12x on a handful of shards. Link: https://grafana/redwood/routers/latency?range=15m
sara: Observed hot partitions: shard-42 and shard-97 in eu-west-2. They have ~3x normal QPS for streaming sessions. Likely routing policy pushed more ephemeral affinity to those shards.
cs-bob: Any customer-visible errors? Support dashboard shows elevated retry rates and some websocket disconnects for customers in EU region. Top impacted tenants: Acme Inc, LumaChat, BrightForms. CS is DMing their account teams.
oncall-amber: Ok plan: 1) stop rollout (prevent further spread) 2) toggle routing policy to previous ordering (immediate rollback via feature flag) 3) drain hot shards / route around them 4) monitor p99/p95 and streaming stall metric. Who can flip the flag?
maria: I can flip the flag. Prepared command:

```bash
# toggle routing policy ordering back to 'legacy-affinity'
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.redwood/api/flags/rb-router-weight-rollout" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"policy_order": "legacy-affinity", "target": "eu-west-2", "apply_immediately": true}'
```

maria: Executing now.
infra-bot: Feature flag change applied by maria at +7m. Rolling back partial canary to legacy ordering for eu-west-2.
dinesh: Good. Also suggest temporary reduce weight for shards 42/97 to avoid hot-cold amplification:

```json
{"shard_adjust": [{"id": 42, "weight": 0.3}, {"id": 97, "weight": 0.25}], "apply": "immediate"}
```

kevin: I applied the weight adjustment. Command: `rbctl shard adjust --id=42 --weight=0.3 && rbctl shard adjust --id=97 --weight=0.25`
oncall-amber: Observability: streaming stalled-sessions metric decreased from 1800 -> 420 in 6 minutes. p99 trending down: 4.5s -> 1.1s. Keep watching.
sara: Traces show far fewer inter-zone hops now. KV cache hit-rate for the hot shards up from 62% -> 85%. Looks like the affinity change was the main factor.
cs-bob: CS: reported tenants are seeing recovery, some clients retried and resumed. Logged incidents for top-3 customers; no data loss; primarily increased latency and disconnects.
infra-bot: Note: rollback prevented rollout to 3 additional eu nodes. No additional regions impacted.
dinesh: Root cause hypothesis: policy reordering in rb-router-weight-rollout prioritized cost-based routing over locality which exposed hot partitioning; hot shards accumulated more streaming sessions, causing local KV cache thrash and cross-shard fanout -> tail stalls.
maria: Agree. Next immediate mitigation: keep legacy ordering for 1h, run targeted reshuffle of affine keys for shards 42/97, and schedule a controlled rollout with canary that injects synthetic traffic to measure tail.
oncall-amber: Who owns postmortem? I’ll take incident writeup with dinesh and sara. Action items:
- amber: write SEV2 incident doc + timeline
- dinesh: collect diffs and PR that changed policy ordering
- sara: produce hotspot heatmap + eviction metrics
- infra: confirm rollback + flag audit entries

kevin: Also add test that simulates skewed key distribution to gating for any future routing policy change.
cs-bob: CS asks for a short blurb for impacted customers: "We experienced elevated latency and websocket disconnects caused by a routing policy change; we rolled back the change and are stabilizing. No data loss; engineers are monitoring. We'll follow up with a timeline and root cause analysis." Approve? :thumbsup:
oncall-amber: Approved, please send.
infra-bot: Audit log: flag rollback recorded (maria, 5510009928). Shard adjustments recorded (kevin, 5510009958).
oncall-amber: Closing bridge in 20m if metrics remain stable. Marking incident as SEV2 -> mitigated. Will open postmortem ticket and schedule 1-hour scrub.
dinesh: Notes for postmortem: include perf tests, gating, and fallback ordering unit tests. Also propose a new canary traffic generator that simulates hot-key churn.
sara: I'll attach flamegraphs and a list of affected prefixes to the postmortem ticket.
cs-bob: CS will send update to customers in 30 minutes with the approved blurb.
oncall-amber: Thanks all. Stand down unless metrics regress. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident 5510009876 status update: mitigated at 5510010200. p99 reduced to <1.2s; streaming stall count down 76%. Postmortem required.
